about: The DD Framework rulebook. Each rule has an id, the incident or source it comes from, the repo kinds it applies to, and two dates: from warn_from it is reported, from enforce_from it fails. enforce_from is at most 90 days after warn_from, so nothing warns forever. lib/rules.mjs holds the checks; test/fixtures.mjs holds a failing and a passing example of every rule, and the tests fail if a rule has none. Exemptions: README, 'Exemptions'.

rules.title: A job in a private Doman-Digital repo names a GitHub-hosted runner directly
rules.why: 2 October 2026: twelve jobs hard-coded to ubuntu-latest used the organisation's hosted minutes and could not move to the self-hosted VM. Use runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}. Only repos owned by Doman-Digital are checked: the runners are registered to the organisation, so a repo in a client's or a personal account cannot use them.

rules.title: A public repo runs jobs on the self-hosted runners
rules.why: GitHub: never use self-hosted runners with public repositories; a fork's pull request could run code on the VM.

rules.title: A job has no timeout-minutes
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was missing-timeout).

rules.title: A pull_request workflow has no concurrency group that cancels superseded runs
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was missing-concurrency).

rules.title: A workflow runs on both push and pull_request for the same branches
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was double-run). Not reported when a workflow_run deploy waits for the workflow: the push run is the deploy's gate, which CI-014 requires on every push to main (DOM-776).

rules.title: continue-on-error: true with no comment saying why
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit: three permanently red jobs ran unnoticed for months (was unexplained-continue-on-error).

rules.title: A scheduled workflow is not registered in budget.yml
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was unregistered-cron). Fixed 2026-10-03: only the first cron under schedule: was ever read.

rules.title: An artifact upload can fail the job when the storage quota is full
rules.why: 2 October 2026: a 360 MB build uploaded on every run used the organisation's artifact storage for the month, and every PR failed at the upload. Pass builds between jobs another way; mark diagnostic uploads continue-on-error with a comment.

rules.title: A vercel.json cron is not registered in budget.yml
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was unregistered-vercel-cron).

rules.title: A run on a push to main is cancelled by the next push
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): dd-relay's CI cancelled its own main run on every merge (group ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true). Deploy waits for a successful CI run, so a burst of merges left nothing deployed and a fix went out hours after it merged. Cancel superseded pull request runs only.

rules.title: A production deploy is not serialised, or can be cancelled halfway
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): a deploy that a newer push cancels can leave a Worker updated and its secrets or migrations not, and two deploys at once can finish in the wrong order. One concurrency group per environment with cancel-in-progress: false; a waiting deploy is still replaced by a newer one.

rules.title: A deploy can ship a commit CI did not test, or one older than main
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): once main CI is never cancelled, several runs finish in any order and each starts a deploy. A deploy checks out the commit its CI run tested (workflow_run.head_sha) and stops when that commit is no longer the tip of main, so the last deploy is always the newest tested commit.

rules.title: A repo that calls the policy check runs its own secret scan on every pull request
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): the monorepo's secret-scan job, redacted' gitleaks.yml, redacted's gitleaks job and redacted's TruffleHog each scanned the same commits as the policy check, a full-history clone and another VM for a one-second scan. The monorepo's alone was about 1,350 VM-minutes a month, on a pool of six VMs.

rules.title: A workflow still works around the persistent runners
rules.why: DOM-555 replaced the eight runners sharing dd-ci-01 with a fresh VM per job. Port offsets from the runner's name, a pnpm folder per runner, workspace clean-ups and hand-off folders on the host now do nothing, or lose what they keep, and the comments around them describe a machine that is gone (DOM-776 audit: the monorepo, redacted, osint-engine, redacted-api).

rules.title: A job that runs on every pull request is allowed to fail
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): visual-regression-portal in the monorepo and osint-engine's integration-tests ran on every PR push with continue-on-error: true. Each took a VM from a pool of six, often for minutes, and a red result changed nothing. Advisory work belongs on a schedule or a manual run.

rules.title: A schedule fires on the hour
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): GitHub started scheduled runs 4 to 9.5 hours late, and its documentation says runs at the start of an hour are the most likely to be delayed or dropped. Crons at minute 0 across the estate then queued together on the shared pool.

rules.title: A scheduled workflow works out its batch from the clock
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): Market-probability-engine's Tiingo batches chose their tickers from the hour the run started. GitHub started the runs hours late, so from 8 October every batch picked an empty slot and refreshed nothing, while every run passed.

rules.title: Three or more pull request jobs each install the same dependencies
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): on the shared pool each job waits for its own VM, then boots, checks out and installs before it does seconds of work. redacted ran 9 to 11 jobs per push, redacted 7, redacted 5, redacted 6, each installing the same lockfile; in the monorepo 58% of job time was setup. One job with several steps does the same checks with one wait and one install.

rules.title: Post-deploy checks start a separate runner for a request
rules.why: DOM-776 audit pattern10: sleeping and requesting DD Checks as a separate reusable-workflow job pays another VM boot and queue wait. Use the composite action as a step after deployment; retain the legacy workflow for callers until they migrate.

rules.title: A third-party action is not pinned to a full commit SHA
rules.why: tj-actions/changed-files, March 2025: a re-pointed tag ran code that dumped CI secrets. GitHub: a full SHA is the only immutable reference. First-party Doman-Digital actions stay on tags.

rules.title: A pnpm repo is missing install protections
rules.why: The 2025 npm worms spread through install scripts and fresh releases. pnpm 10 and later block dependency install scripts unless listed; this rule requires minimumReleaseAge and forbids dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds.

rules.title: No dependency updates configured
rules.why: Security fixes reach a repo only through Renovate (extending this repo's default.json) or Dependabot.

rules.title: A file of secrets is tracked by git
rules.why: 4 October 2026: a pulled env file with 66 production values sat on a client repo's main branch for six months. The CI secret scan only read each push's own commits, so nothing ever looked at it.

rules.title: .gitignore does not cover env and token files
rules.why: 4 October 2026: 12 repos had no .env rule and most client repos did not ignore .doppler-token, while a bulk `git add` stages everything.

rules.title: Nothing scans pull requests for secrets
rules.why: 4 October 2026: GitHub secret scanning is a paid add-on for private repos and was off everywhere; a live Stripe key reached a pushed branch the same day.

rules.title: A Cloudflare deploy reads its token from a GitHub secret
rules.why: 6 and 7 October 2026: the security review found broad, non-expiring Cloudflare tokens hand-copied into repo secrets, where nothing rotates or audits them. Since 13 October 2026 (DOM-776) Workers deploy from Actions through cloudflare-deploy.yml, which fetches a narrow, expiring, per-account token from Doppler with the repo's GitHub identity. Simple static client sites may instead deploy through Cloudflare's GitHub app (Workers Builds), which leaves no token with us.

rules.title: A workflow has no explicit top-level token permissions
rules.why: DOM-776 audit pattern15: workflows inherited unspecified repository token permissions. Declare the minimum top-level permissions (an empty map is valid), and grant any extra permission only to the job that needs it.

rules.title: A Worker has no registered deploy path, or two
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): some Workers were built by Cloudflare's GitHub app, some by Actions, and seven repos had no trace of how they deploy. deploys.json lists every Worker with its one path: Actions (cloudflare-deploy.yml) for internal Workers and anything gated, Workers Builds only for simple static client sites, or retired.

rules.title: The repo runs a craft catalogue older than copy-check trusts
rules.why: 19 October 2026: copy-check passed a client email full of chatbot residue because the machine ran craft catalogue 2026.09.12. Repos were worse: their lockfiles held craft 0.5.0 to 0.20.2 (catalogues none to 2026.10.2) while npm had 0.20.5, because Renovate aborted every repo before opening a PR (DOM-1043). The floor is floors.json, the same number copy-check refuses below. Renovate's house packages group bumps craft within a day of a release; a repo still behind fails here rather than checking copy with old rules.

rules.title: The repo's description or tags break repo-topics.json
rules.why: Every repo must be identifiable from its GitHub page alone, and its kind tag decides which rules apply (was the repo metadata check, enforced since September 2026).

rules.title: The repo has workflows but none calls the policy check
rules.why: 3 October 2026: 14 of 48 repos with workflows were checked by nothing.

rules.title: Auto-merge or delete-branch-on-merge is off
rules.why: 7 October 2026: pull requests are assessed and merged by agents, with the required checks as the only gate (DOM-443). Auto-merge lets a PR merge itself the moment its checks pass, and deleting the branch on merge stops merged branches piling up. Both are repo settings, read from GitHub; when the settings cannot be read, nothing is checked. Auto-merge is not required on a private repo in a personal account, where GitHub's Free plan ignores it; delete-branch-on-merge still is.

rules.title: An exemption expires within 14 days, is invalid, or exempts nothing
rules.why: Exemptions expire so ignored debt comes back as a finding instead of a forgotten note. One that matches no finding hides the next real one unreviewed (DOM-776 audit, 13 October 2026: dd-seo-mcp, dd-repo-registry and dd-prompt-library carried exemptions for findings already fixed).

rules.title: The repo pins dd-ci-standards to one release instead of v1
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): Renovate rewrote @v1 to fixed releases. policy.yml itself ran the doctor at v1.0.13 from 5 October, so every PR gate missed SEC-007, REG-004 and the CI-001 fixes while v1 had moved on to v1.0.22.
